localNote: The Flying Standard on Trinity Street and the Earl of Mercia on High Street are both in the compact city centre, a short stroll from the cathedral ruins and the Lady Godiva statue. Note that the Spon Gate at the SkyDome was reported closed in 2025, so check before heading there.

pubs.name: The Flying Standard
pubs.history: Named after the Flying Standard cars built in Coventry from 1936 until the Second World War. The mock-Tudor building dates from 1938 to 1939 and once housed a Timothy Whites chemist.

pubs.name: The Earl of Mercia
pubs.history: Opened in 1896 as a London and Midland Bank branch. The name honours Leofric, Earl of Mercia, founder of St Mary's Priory and husband of Lady Godiva.

pubs.name: The Spon Gate
pubs.history: Named after one of the gates in Coventry's medieval city walls, which stood on Spon Street until 1771. The pub occupied a former Chicago Rock Cafe in the SkyDome complex from 2010.
